siding_exposure_m.note: INVENTED WITHIN A STOCK SET, NOT DERIVED. No source states the exposed face of any Chicago building's siding. The value is one of four period mill sidings — 4.5, 5, 5.5 or 6 in to the weather; this roof wears 6 in — dealt in this building's own parcel recipe: drawn from the set on this record's stable key, then advanced so that no roof of the parcel standing within 60 m hangs the same course. It is NOT keyed to a construction season the way the named buildings' stocks are: this record's 1835-01-01 is the programme's count-unit convention and not a date anything was built, so keying to it would deal every anonymous roof in the town one stock. The separation is the surface variety T-0049 reconstructs, not a claim about 1835. docs/LIBERTIES.md L148 owns the invention and the recipe half is recorded beside it, under `tools/siding_stock.py`.

occupants.note: ADOPTED BY THE INFERRED-HOUSEHOLD PROGRAMME (docs/ROADMAP.md K1, phase two). This anonymous roof is the dwelling of an inferred domestic's household (1 of 4 this layer infers): hh_inf_domestic_north_01 in data/residents/households/. THE ROOF'S OWN EXISTENCE, POSITION AND FOOTPRINT REMAIN CONJECTURAL and are unchanged by the adoption; what the adoption adds is an argued occupant instead of an anonymous count-unit. The occupant is hypothesised from the town's demonstrable needs - the 1835 census of 3,265 people in 398 dwellings against the trades Andreas's 1833 roster names - and is not a person: no name is claimed and no figure is drawn.

residents.name: The McGuire household — a reconstructed domestic (north division)
residents.why: THE HOUSEHOLD IS HOUSED, WHICH IS THE POINT OF THE LAYER. recon_1835_north_d3_042 is an anonymous reconstructed roof already standing on the plat, adopted rather than duplicated: its existence, position and footprint stay conjectural and the adoption adds only the occupant argument. Which roof of the right family and district a hypothesised household occupies is not evidence about that roof; the household needed a dwelling and the programme assigned it one.
residents.basis: An anonymous roof of the reconstruction programme, ADOPTED by this household rather than raised for it. The roof's own existence and position stay conjectural; what the adoption adds is an argued occupant instead of an anonymous count-unit.

persons.name: Mary McGuire
persons.note: HYPOTHESISED, AND NOT A PERSON. No source names this resident and none is claimed to: the record asserts that a town of 3,265 people in 398 dwellings held at least this many households of this trade, and asserts nothing whatever about any individual. THE NAME IS INVENTED TOO, and `name_basis` beside it says so and says which pool it came from: this record used to carry a bare designation instead, on the reasoning that a surname would make it look like the documented layer, but a town of designations does not read as a town and the grade, this note and name_basis all say plainly which layer this is. No figure is drawn (docs/LIBERTIES.md L1). THE FIRST OF 4 DOMESTIC HOUSEHOLDS THIS LAYER RECONSTRUCTS. The same argument and the same silence. Four domestic households are inferred as households in their own right rather than as servants attached to named families, because attaching an invented servant to a documented household would put a fabricated person inside a real one. SEX IS STATED HERE AND NOWHERE ELSE IN THIS LAYER: the argument for the trade is explicitly an argument about women's work, so recording the person as male would contradict the reasoning that produced her.

residents.research_note: RECONSTRUCTED HOUSEHOLD - first of 4 domestic households in this layer, in the north division. The same argument and the same silence. Four domestic households are inferred as households in their own right rather than as servants attached to named families, because attaching an invented servant to a documented household would put a fabricated person inside a real one. METHOD: the count comes from the occupation census in data/reconstruction/1835_inferred_household_programme.json, which calibrates every trade against three things this project already holds - the 1835 town census (3,265 people, 398 dwellings), Andreas's roster of the fall of 1833 (about fifty named people, most with a trade, in a settlement of some 350), and the reconstruction specification's roof schedule, whose workshop and store family targets are treated as the ceiling on a trade rather than as its measure. Every count is stated NET of the documented layer: this dataset infers a tradesman only where it cannot name one.
